items.finding: The definition of Confidential Information is clear and specific, indicating that it includes any non-public information disclosed in connection with the Purpose.
items.quote: any non-public information disclosed by a Party (the ”Disclosing Party”) to the other Party (the ”Receiving Party”) in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential, including sales and customer data, supplier terms, pricing, product roadmaps, solution designs, source code and methodologies.
items.counterPosition: The definition could be more specific regarding the types of information that are considered confidential. For example, it could include specific examples of confidential information, such as customer lists or trade secrets.

items.finding: The obligations of the Parties are clear, indicating that each Party is responsible for protecting the Confidential Information of the other Party.
items.quote: The Receiving Party shall: (a) use the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information only for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its employees, directors, professional advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Agreement; (c) protect it with at least reasonable care and no less care than it applies to its own confidential information; and (d) promptly notify the Disclosing Party of any unauthorised use or disclosure of which it becomes aware.
items.counterPosition: The obligations could be more specific regarding the scope of the Parties' responsibilities. For example, it could include specific examples of when the Parties are responsible for protecting the Confidential Information.

items.finding: The residuals clause is clear, indicating that the Parties retain ownership of their Confidential Information and are not granted any licence to use it.
items.quote: Confidential Information remains the property of the Disclosing Party. No licence is granted except the limited right to use it for the Purpose.
items.counterPosition: The residuals clause could be more specific regarding the scope of the Parties' rights. For example, it could include specific examples of when the Parties can use their Confidential Information.

items.finding: The remedies clause is clear, indicating that the Parties acknowledge that damages may not be an adequate remedy for breach and that the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to other remedies available at law.
items.quote: Each Party acknowledges that damages may not be an adequate remedy for breach, and the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to other remedies available at law.
items.counterPosition: The remedies clause could be more specific regarding the scope of the Parties' rights. For example, it could include specific examples of when the Disclosing Party can seek injunctive relief.

items.finding: The covenants clause is clear, indicating that the Parties agree to certain non-compete and non-solicit provisions.
items.quote: Neither Party is obliged to enter into any further agreement. Each Party remains free to work with third parties, provided it does not use or disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information.
items.counterPosition: The covenants clause could be more specific regarding the scope of the Parties' obligations. For example, it could include specific examples of when the Parties are bound by the non-compete and non-solicit provisions.

items.finding: The term clause is clear, indicating that the Agreement remains in force for two years from the Effective Date and that the Parties' obligations continue for three years after expiry or termination of the Agreement.
items.quote: This Agreement remains in force for two (2) years from the Effective Date. Either Party may terminate it earlier on thirty (30) days’ written notice.
items.counterPosition: The term clause could be more specific regarding the scope of the Parties' obligations. For example, it could include specific examples of when the Parties' obligations continue after expiry or termination of the Agreement.
